1	# Plan: run `local-llms/local-llm` on NVIDIA DGX Spark through a multi-arch image
2	
3	Status: proposed, not implemented. Revised 2026-09-28 after two reviews of version `a8f8085b…`:
4	
5	- `plans/local-llm-multiarch-plan-review-claude-code-opus-5-5.md` (findings F1–F15);
6	- `plans/local-llm-multiarch-plan-review-codex-gpt-6_codex.md` (findings 1–11).
7	
8	Section 8 maps each finding to the change it caused.
9	
10	## 1. Goal
11	
12	Make the existing Ploinky agent `local-llms/local-llm` run local LLMs on an NVIDIA DGX Spark, optimized for that machine, without breaking it on the x86 hosts it serves today. Explorer (AssistOSExplorer) must keep enabling one agent, and Ploinky must not learn anything about the `local-llms` repository.
13	
14	## 2. Decision
15	
16	- **One agent,** `local-llms/local-llm`. No separate `dgx-local-llm` agent. Both reviews found no evidence against this.
17	- **A multi-arch image.** The agent's image becomes an OCI index, published like `ploinky-node` and `ploinky-box`:
18	  - `linux/amd64`: today's image, unchanged. Its manifest digest `sha256:b6c79af2aad08b542339346f4a985c84d5cbcacc31e8c6df45f951da7ba0fbf7` is reused as-is inside the index (B1).
19	  - `linux/arm64`: a new build for the GB10 GPU (compute capability 12.1). The agent reports other arm64 NVIDIA GPUs (GH200, Jetson Thor) as unsupported by this image (C4).
20	- **A hardware profile chosen at run time.** The agent picks dedicated or unified memory from what `nvidia-smi` reports (C1). The JavaScript source is shared by both architectures, because Ploinky mounts the agent directory at `/code`; only binaries and locks come from the image.
21	- **One agent left in the repository.** The twelve legacy shared-image agents (a manager and eleven model agents) are deleted (D).
22	
23	### Alternatives considered and rejected
24	
25	| Alternative | Why rejected |
26	| --- | --- |
27	| Two agents (`local-llm` + `dgx-local-llm`) chosen per host by a new Ploinky feature (agent-declared `hostRequirements`, an `if-supported` enable modifier and a host-facts file written into the Box) | Needs a Ploinky feature, Explorer plugin filtering (Explorer aggregates `IDE-plugins/` from every agent in installed repos, enabled or not), and duplicated code. A multi-arch index selects the right image with no new mechanism. |
28	| Fork `local-llm` into a new agent | About 13k lines copied to change about 1k (estimate from a module-by-module audit). |
29	| `profiles.<profile>.enable` | The operator chooses the profile; it does not detect the host. |
30	| Ploinky DS014 `llmRuntime` architecture catalog | Selects an image for one agent, depends on an external catalog, and its policies (`--gpus`, host IPC) are refused inside the Box. |
31	| A default manifest platform of `linux/amd64` | Would refuse every agent without the field on arm64 hosts, including the ~15 `ploinky-node` agents already running on this Spark. The default must stay today's behaviour: the host's own platform. |
32	
33	## 3. Facts this plan relies on
34	
35	The reviews verified these on 2026-09-28: on this host, through registry and PyPI metadata, and in upstream sources at the pinned tags. Each review's fact-check table gives the evidence. Anything marked "Phase 0" or "Phase 1" is still open and is settled by that phase.
36	
37	### Host (this machine)
38	
39	| Fact | How to check |
40	| --- | --- |
41	| NVIDIA DGX Spark (Lenovo OEM, `30KL0004GF`); DGX OS 7.2.3 base build with OTA 7.5.0; Ubuntu 24.04.4; kernel 6.17; aarch64 | `cat /etc/dgx-release; uname -a` |
42	| NVIDIA GB10, PCI device ID `0x2E1210DE`, compute capability 12.1, driver 580.159.03, CUDA 13.0 | `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,pci.device_id,compute_cap,driver_version --format=csv` |
43	| `nvidia-smi` reports `memory.total/used/free` as `[N/A]` and `addressing_mode` as `ATS`. Utilization, power, temperature and per-process `used_memory` are numeric. | `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total,addressing_mode,utilization.gpu,power.draw,temperature.gpu --format=csv`; `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory --format=csv` |
44	| 119.6 GiB MemTotal, no swap | `free -h` |
45	| 20 cores: 10 Cortex-X925 (cpu5–9 and 15–19, sysfs `cpu_capacity` 997–1024) and 10 Cortex-A725 (cpu0–4 and 10–14, 718–731); no SME | `lscpu; cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpu_capacity` |
46	| 1 TB NVMe with about 132 GB free, shared with the live workspace (85 % used) | `df -h /` |
47	| Single Spark; all ConnectX-7 ports down | `ip -br link; ibdev2netdev` |
48	| Host tools: CUDA 13.0.88, cmake 3.28.3, gcc 13.3. cmake 3.28 accepts `121a-real`; only the `f` suffixes need 3.31.8+. gcc 13.3 cannot resolve `-mcpu=native` on this CPU and falls back to baseline armv8-a. | `nvcc --version; cmake --version; gcc -mcpu=native -Q --help=target` |
49	| nvidia-container-toolkit 1.19.1 is installed, so GPU containers run on the host without Ploinky | `nvidia-ctk --version` |
50	
51	### GB10 memory behaviour
52	
53	These were measured on 2026-09-28 with small CUDA test programs on the host. Phase 1 repeats the measurements inside a nested agent container.
54	
55	- **Integrated device.** CUDA reports the device as integrated: `integrated=1`, `pageableMemoryAccessUsesHostPageTables=1`, and 119.63 GiB total.
56	- **`cudaMemGetInfo` reports MemFree, not MemAvailable.** It returned 48.2 GiB free while MemAvailable was 106.3 GiB and 53.9 GiB was page cache.
57	- **CUDA allocations reclaim clean page cache.** 56 GiB was allocated and touched starting from 48 GiB of MemFree, and Cached fell by 9.8 GiB.
58	- **The runners size from MemAvailable.** On integrated GPUs, llama.cpp b11159 (its fit logic), Ollama 0.34.4 and vLLM 0.30.0 (`psutil.virtual_memory().available`) all do.
59	- **Allocation is fast.** Allocating and first touching memory runs at about 28 GiB/s.
60	- **GPU memory is invisible to per-process accounting.**
61	  - A process holding 4 GiB had 98 MB of RSS and the baseline `oom_score`.
62	  - Inside a `MemoryMax=2G` scope, its cgroup showed 70 MiB.
63	  - So neither the kernel OOM killer's choice of victim nor memory cgroups see GPU allocations.
64	
65	### Current failure
66	
67	- Explorer's manifest enables `local-llms/local-llm no-wait` (`.ploinky/repos/AchillesIDE/explorer/manifest.json:28`, `enable` list).
68	- On this host the Box pulled the amd64-only `local-llm` image (4.57 GB, 620 s). The runtime-key probe then failed with `Exec format error` (`ploinky/cli/utils/dependencies/dependencyRuntimeKey.js:151`).
69	  - The dead 4.91 GB image stays in the Box's image store.
70	  - Log: `/home/research/work/.ploinky/logs/no-wait/ploinky_local-llms_local-llm_work_287e1573.*.log`.
71	- `ploinky gpu status` fails on this host. Run it from `/home/research/work` as `/home/research/work/ploinky/bin/ploinky gpu status`, because `ploinky` is not on PATH.
72	  - It reports `Host GPU: unavailable (NVIDIA driver library libcuda.so.1 is not in the ldconfig cache)`.
73	  - Cause: `parseLdconfigCache` accepts only entries flagged `x86-64` (`ploinky/ploinky-box/gpuGrant.mjs:239`), and on this host the flag is `AArch64`.
74	  - With only that filter changed, the rest of discovery succeeds here: 3 device nodes, 5 driver libraries and `nvidia-smi`.
75	  - The CDI spec, fingerprint and marker carry no architecture data.
76	- If the agent did run here, admission would pass every model on GPU memory.
77	  - `readGpu` (`local-llm/src/controller/hardware.mjs`) turns `[N/A]` into `NaN`, so every GPU-memory comparison in `src/controller/admission.mjs` is false.
78	  - A 500 GiB GGUF (llama.cpp) and a 400 GiB tag (Ollama) are admitted. RAM and disk checks still apply.
79	  - vLLM gets a `NaN` GPU share and fails at launch (`src/runners/vllm.mjs:115-117`), unless an admin sets the share.
80	
81	### Multi-arch mechanics
82	
83	- **`ploinky-node` is an index.** Explorer pins `ploinky-node` by digest `sha256:accd925f…` (`explorer/manifest.json:2`). That digest is an OCI image index with `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` entries, and podman on this Spark resolved it to arm64.
84	- **`local-llm` is a single manifest.**
85	  - Its manifest pins a single amd64 image manifest, `b6c79…`, with revision label `95ba10a…`.
86	  - It was pushed with `provenance: false`, and the OCI referrers API lists no attestations for it.
87	  - The publish workflow's candidate step already wraps it in an index (`candidate-36131512550-1`), so an `imagetools create` of it plus an arm64 digest is a known operation.
88	- **Pulls use the host platform.** Ploinky runs `podman pull <image>` with no `--platform` (`ploinky/cli/sandbox/docker/common.js:196`). It adds `--platform` only when `llmRuntime.runtimePolicy.platform` is set (`ploinky/cli/sandbox/docker/containerRuntimePolicy.js:262`).
89	- **The `ploinky-node` workflow is the model.** `container-image-builds/.github/workflows/publish-ploinky-node-image.yml` builds each platform on its native runner (`ubuntu-24.04`, `ubuntu-24.04-arm`), pushes by digest, proves each platform, and then assembles the index with `docker buildx imagetools create`.
90	- **Where the amd64 lock-in is.** The runtime base `ploinky-node:24-trixie-tools@sha256:accd925f…` is that same multi-arch index. The amd64 lock-in is the guard `test "${TARGETARCH:-amd64}" = amd64` (`container-image-builds/images/local-llm/Dockerfile:54`) and the x64 downloads that follow it.
91	- **The dependency cache needs no change.**
92	  - Ploinky keys it by the image's own `process.arch` (`container-linux-arm64-glibc-node24` vs `container-linux-x64-glibc-node24`).
93	  - The pin change invalidates each host's cache once, because the stamp records the image reference.
94	
95	### Box
96	
97	- **Image.** `ploinky-box:latest` is a multi-arch index; its arm64 variant runs on this Spark (Fedora 44, podman 5.8.2).
98	- **GPU wiring.**
99	  - The Box image contains no NVIDIA userland.
100	  - GPU wiring consists of device nodes, read-only binds of the host's driver libraries under `/usr/local/nvidia`, a hookless CDI spec `ploinky.local/gpu=all`, and a grant marker.
101	  - The wiring is fixed when the Box is created.
102	- **Code vs create arguments.**
103	  - The Box mounts the host's Ploinky checkout read-only at `/opt/ploinky`, so Ploinky code changes reach the Box without an image rebuild.
104	  - New GPU wiring or Box create arguments take effect only when the Box is replaced, and that restarts the workspace's agents.
105	- **Constraints for agents:**
106	  - no `--ipc host`;
107	  - `/dev/shm` at most `16g`;
108	  - one 2,048-task pid limit shared by every agent (727 in use with 15 agents);
109	  - nested cgroups disabled, and the Box itself has no memory limit;
110	  - no host networking or RDMA (multi-Spark is out of scope by design).
111	- **Not yet tested.** Nested CDI on arm64 is untested, because the Box has no GPU wiring today (Phase 1).
112	
113	### Runner availability on arm64
114	
115	**llama.cpp b11159** (tag commit `6b790a9c291b5d7af3312bbf9f0c558aa023b13e`):
116	
117	- **Prebuilt assets.** `llama-b11159-bin-ubuntu-cuda-13.4-arm64.tar.gz` (sha256 `258c9dc7c6c02fd2d805ebf9511876ab7b9d7b2d3f0c2166454d682ccae7644b`) and `cudart-llama-b11159-bin-ubuntu-cuda-13.4-arm64.tar.gz` (`34d8602d0084b2498dbf0c436fe2d1d4e54ba577b8d5567eb56990e8fff11bfa`; cudart, cuBLAS and cuBLASLt `.so.13`).
118	- **How the prebuilt is built.** On `ubuntu-24.04-arm`, in `nvidia/cuda:13.4.1-devel-ubuntu24.04`, with gcc-14 and `GGML_NATIVE=OFF GGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS=ON GGML_BACKEND_DL=ON`. It sets no `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES`, so the default list applies: `75-virtual;80-virtual;86-real;89-real;90-virtual;120a-real;121a-real`, which includes native `sm_121a` code.
119	- **Driver compatibility.** CUDA 13.x applications run on driver ≥ 580 under minor-version compatibility, provided no PTX JIT is needed. The forward-compatibility package does not apply to GB10.
120	- **CPU code.** On this CPU (no SME), the `armv8.6_2` variant is selected.
121	- **CCCL.** A CUDA 13.0 build ships CCCL 3.0.1 and so loses the CUB top-k path, which needs CCCL ≥ 3.2 and which 13.4 has.
122	- **Still open (Phase 0).** The cubins actually inside the shipped `libggml-cuda.so`, and a run on this driver.
123	
124	**llama.cpp b11159 options:**
125	
126	- **Load mode.**
127	  - `--no-mmap`, `--mmap`, `--mlock` and `--direct-io` were removed in b10875. The option is now `--load-mode {auto,none,mmap,mlock,mmap+mlock,dio}`.
128	  - `auto` already avoids mmap on an integrated GPU.
129	  - `dio` reads with O_DIRECT; ggml-org's Spark benchmark uses `mmap 0, dio 1`.
130	- **Defaults.** `--jinja` is on by default. `-np` defaults to 4 slots with a unified KV cache.
131	- **MTP exists.** `--spec-type draft-mtp` and `--spec-draft-n-max` (default 3).
132	- **Mixed KV types are slow.** Flash-attention kernels are compiled only for same-type K/V pairs; a mixed pair converts to f16.
133	- **Build identity.** Without git metadata a build reports build 0 and commit `unknown`, unless `LLAMA_BUILD_NUMBER` and `LLAMA_BUILD_COMMIT` are set (`cmake/build-info.cmake`).
134	
135	**NVIDIA's llama.cpp playbook** (`NVIDIA/dgx-spark-playbooks`, `nvidia/llama-cpp`, updated 06/03/2026):
136	
137	- It clones llama.cpp master without a pin and builds with the host toolkit: `-DGGML_NATIVE=ON -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DGGML_CURL=ON -DGGML_RPC=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=121a-real`. `GGML_CURL` is not an option at b11159.
138	- It runs with the defaults plus the MTP flags and `--chat-template-kwargs '{"preserve_thinking": true}'`.
139	
140	**Ollama v0.34.4:**
141	
142	- **Asset.** `ollama-linux-arm64.tar.zst`: 1,549,684,612 bytes, sha256 `96f50a1192133028cf4e010d8c333f8af14b1505db6be7b2034c11487e7fd7e6`. GB10 is listed as supported.
143	- **No native sm_121 code.** `cuda_v12` has `sm_120a`, which runs only on 12.0, and `cuda_v13` is PTX-only (`compute_121a`). So the driver JIT-compiles it on first load.
144	- **Memory.** On integrated GPUs it sizes from MemAvailable and loads with `--load-mode dio`.
145	- **Install route.** NVIDIA's Ollama playbook installs the unpinned `install.sh`.
146	- **Still open.** Untested on this host (Phase 0).
147	
148	**vLLM 0.30.0** (installed on demand):
149	
150	- **Wheels.**
151	  - The wheel is `vllm-0.30.0-cp38-abi3-manylinux_2_28_aarch64.whl`.
152	  - All 196 distributions in the amd64 lock have cp313 aarch64 wheels at the same versions on `files.pythonhosted.org`: none is sdist-only, 3.94 GB in total.
153	  - torch 2.13 depends on `cuda-toolkit[…]==13.0.3`.
154	- **Kernels.**
155	  - vLLM's NVFP4, FP8, Marlin and MoE kernels are built for `12.0f`, which covers 12.1.
156	  - FlashAttention 2 is PTX only, so the driver JIT-compiles it.
157	  - torch ships `sm_120` machine code.
158	  - Triton 3.7.1 maps 12.1 to `sm_121a`, bundles ptxas 13.1.80 and links `-l:libcuda.so.1`.
159	- **FlashInfer.**
160	  - FlashInfer 0.6.18 needs a CUDA toolkit (nvcc on PATH) at run time, so offline vLLM turns it off.
161	  - When the network is reachable, vLLM probes NVIDIA's artifactory to decide FlashInfer paths on SM12x.
162	- **Known issue.** gpt-oss uses Marlin MXFP4 on SM121, and vLLM #37030 (wrong first Harmony token) is open.
163	- **Still open.** Untested on this host (Phase 4).
164	
165	**ik_llama.cpp, TabbyAPI and LM Studio:** x86-only builds today; left out of arm64.
166	
167	### Model sizes (Hugging Face, for disk planning)
168	
169	| Model | Size |
170	| --- | --- |
171	| gpt-oss-20b MXFP4 GGUF | 12.1 GB |
172	| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MTP GGUF, UD-Q4_K_XL / Q8_0 | 22.9 / 37.8 GB |
173	| Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B Q8_0 | 32.5 GB |
174	| GLM-4.7-Flash Q8_0 | 31.8 GB |
175	| gpt-oss-120b MXFP4 GGUF | 63.4 GB, one file |
176	| Qwen3.5-122B-A10B MXFP4_MOE | 74.7 GB, 3 files |
177	| `openai/gpt-oss-120b` safetensors (for vLLM) | 65.2 GB |
178	
179	### Consumer side
180	
181	- **Discovery.** Soul Gateway discovers the agent through the Router's `/api/router/openai-agent-discovery` and names the model `local-llms/local-llm/default`. It already supports several models per agent through `endpoints.models.command` (later phase).
182	- **Deadlines.** The chat endpoint's command limit is 600 s (`manifest.json` `timeoutMs: 600000`). Soul Gateway's default request deadline is 120 s.
183	- **Request fields.** Soul Gateway drops `reasoning_content` and `reasoning_effort` and forwards only some sampling fields. These are later-phase gateway patches, unless decision 9 moves them earlier.
184	
185	## 4. Work by repository
186	
187	### A. Ploinky (`github.com/AssistOS-AI/ploinky`) — prerequisite
188	
189	**1. Required: `parseLdconfigCache` accepts the ldconfig flag of the host architecture.**
190	
191	- `x64` maps to `x86-64` and `arm64` to `AArch64`; an unknown architecture is refused with a clear reason.
192	- `discoverNvidiaGpu` takes `arch`, defaulting to `process.arch`.
193	- Tests pass the architecture explicitly:
194	  - x64 and arm64 fixtures;
195	  - an arm64 cache that also lists x86-64 or 32-bit entries;
196	  - whitespace in the flags;
197	  - missing libraries, a version mismatch, and an unknown architecture;
198	  - a round-trip of the arm64 CDI spec, marker and fingerprint that adds no device, mount or privilege.
199	- Fix the comment at `gpuGrant.mjs:232`; the README has no x86-64 wording.
200	- **Rollout.** A workspace gets GPU wiring at its next Box replacement (`ploinky start`, `restart` or `update`), which restarts its agents. Do it first in a separate test workspace (Phase 1), then in the live workspace (Phase 3).
201	
202	**2. Optional, with A1: bind `libnvidia-nvvm70.so.4` when present.** Treat it as a soname-specific exception to the check that driver libraries carry the driver version in their file names: its real file is unversioned, and `libcuda` names it. It exists on every R580 host, x86 included; llama.cpp does not need it.
203	
204	**3. Only if Phase 4 measures a need: raise the Box's 2,048-task pid limit.** It is a Box create argument, so every workspace's Box is replaced, and Ploinky's Box-identity and E2E rules apply. Keep it a separate change from A1.
205	
206	**4. Optional: refuse an image before pulling it** when its index has no entry for the host platform, or when it is a single-platform image for another platform, instead of pulling it and failing with `Exec format error`.
207	
208	- No manifest field; the default stays the host's own platform.

# Plan: run `local-llms/local-llm` on NVIDIA DGX Spark through a multi-arch image

Status: proposed, not implemented. Revised 2026-09-28 after two reviews of version `a8f8085b…`:

- `plans/local-llm-multiarch-plan-review-claude-code-opus-5-5.md` (findings F1–F15);
- `plans/local-llm-multiarch-plan-review-codex-gpt-6_codex.md` (findings 1–11).

Section 8 maps each finding to the change it caused.

## 1. Goal

Make the existing Ploinky agent `local-llms/local-llm` run local LLMs on an NVIDIA DGX Spark, optimized for that machine, without breaking it on the x86 hosts it serves today. Explorer (AssistOSExplorer) must keep enabling one agent, and Ploinky must not learn anything about the `local-llms` repository.

## 2. Decision

- **One agent,** `local-llms/local-llm`. No separate `dgx-local-llm` agent. Both reviews found no evidence against this.
- **A multi-arch image.** The agent's image becomes an OCI index, published like `ploinky-node` and `ploinky-box`:
  - `linux/amd64`: today's image, unchanged. Its manifest digest `sha256:b6c79af2aad08b542339346f4a985c84d5cbcacc31e8c6df45f951da7ba0fbf7` is reused as-is inside the index (B1).
  - `linux/arm64`: a new build for the GB10 GPU (compute capability 12.1). The agent reports other arm64 NVIDIA GPUs (GH200, Jetson Thor) as unsupported by this image (C4).
- **A hardware profile chosen at run time.** The agent picks dedicated or unified memory from what `nvidia-smi` reports (C1). The JavaScript source is shared by both architectures, because Ploinky mounts the agent directory at `/code`; only binaries and locks come from the image.
- **One agent left in the repository.** The twelve legacy shared-image agents (a manager and eleven model agents) are deleted (D).

### Alternatives considered and rejected

| Alternative | Why rejected |
| --- | --- |
| Two agents (`local-llm` + `dgx-local-llm`) chosen per host by a new Ploinky feature (agent-declared `hostRequirements`, an `if-supported` enable modifier and a host-facts file written into the Box) | Needs a Ploinky feature, Explorer plugin filtering (Explorer aggregates `IDE-plugins/` from every agent in installed repos, enabled or not), and duplicated code. A multi-arch index selects the right image with no new mechanism. |
| Fork `local-llm` into a new agent | About 13k lines copied to change about 1k (estimate from a module-by-module audit). |
| `profiles.<profile>.enable` | The operator chooses the profile; it does not detect the host. |
| Ploinky DS014 `llmRuntime` architecture catalog | Selects an image for one agent, depends on an external catalog, and its policies (`--gpus`, host IPC) are refused inside the Box. |
| A default manifest platform of `linux/amd64` | Would refuse every agent without the field on arm64 hosts, including the ~15 `ploinky-node` agents already running on this Spark. The default must stay today's behaviour: the host's own platform. |

## 3. Facts this plan relies on

The reviews verified these on 2026-09-28: on this host, through registry and PyPI metadata, and in upstream sources at the pinned tags. Each review's fact-check table gives the evidence. Anything marked "Phase 0" or "Phase 1" is still open and is settled by that phase.

### Host (this machine)

| Fact | How to check |
| --- | --- |
| NVIDIA DGX Spark (Lenovo OEM, `30KL0004GF`); DGX OS 7.2.3 base build with OTA 7.5.0; Ubuntu 24.04.4; kernel 6.17; aarch64 | `cat /etc/dgx-release; uname -a` |
| NVIDIA GB10, PCI device ID `0x2E1210DE`, compute capability 12.1, driver 580.159.03, CUDA 13.0 | `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,pci.device_id,compute_cap,driver_version --format=csv` |
| `nvidia-smi` reports `memory.total/used/free` as `[N/A]` and `addressing_mode` as `ATS`. Utilization, power, temperature and per-process `used_memory` are numeric. | `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total,addressing_mode,utilization.gpu,power.draw,temperature.gpu --format=csv`; `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory --format=csv` |
| 119.6 GiB MemTotal, no swap | `free -h` |
| 20 cores: 10 Cortex-X925 (cpu5–9 and 15–19, sysfs `cpu_capacity` 997–1024) and 10 Cortex-A725 (cpu0–4 and 10–14, 718–731); no SME | `lscpu; cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpu_capacity` |
| 1 TB NVMe with about 132 GB free, shared with the live workspace (85 % used) | `df -h /` |
| Single Spark; all ConnectX-7 ports down | `ip -br link; ibdev2netdev` |
| Host tools: CUDA 13.0.88, cmake 3.28.3, gcc 13.3. cmake 3.28 accepts `121a-real`; only the `f` suffixes need 3.31.8+. gcc 13.3 cannot resolve `-mcpu=native` on this CPU and falls back to baseline armv8-a. | `nvcc --version; cmake --version; gcc -mcpu=native -Q --help=target` |
| nvidia-container-toolkit 1.19.1 is installed, so GPU containers run on the host without Ploinky | `nvidia-ctk --version` |

### GB10 memory behaviour

These were measured on 2026-09-28 with small CUDA test programs on the host. Phase 1 repeats the measurements inside a nested agent container.

- **Integrated device.** CUDA reports the device as integrated: `integrated=1`, `pageableMemoryAccessUsesHostPageTables=1`, and 119.63 GiB total.
- **`cudaMemGetInfo` reports MemFree, not MemAvailable.** It returned 48.2 GiB free while MemAvailable was 106.3 GiB and 53.9 GiB was page cache.
- **CUDA allocations reclaim clean page cache.** 56 GiB was allocated and touched starting from 48 GiB of MemFree, and Cached fell by 9.8 GiB.
- **The runners size from MemAvailable.** On integrated GPUs, llama.cpp b11159 (its fit logic), Ollama 0.34.4 and vLLM 0.30.0 (`psutil.virtual_memory().available`) all do.
- **Allocation is fast.** Allocating and first touching memory runs at about 28 GiB/s.
- **GPU memory is invisible to per-process accounting.**
  - A process holding 4 GiB had 98 MB of RSS and the baseline `oom_score`.
  - Inside a `MemoryMax=2G` scope, its cgroup showed 70 MiB.
  - So neither the kernel OOM killer's choice of victim nor memory cgroups see GPU allocations.

### Current failure

- Explorer's manifest enables `local-llms/local-llm no-wait` (`.ploinky/repos/AchillesIDE/explorer/manifest.json:28`, `enable` list).
- On this host the Box pulled the amd64-only `local-llm` image (4.57 GB, 620 s). The runtime-key probe then failed with `Exec format error` (`ploinky/cli/utils/dependencies/dependencyRuntimeKey.js:151`).
  - The dead 4.91 GB image stays in the Box's image store.
  - Log: `/home/research/work/.ploinky/logs/no-wait/ploinky_local-llms_local-llm_work_287e1573.*.log`.
- `ploinky gpu status` fails on this host. Run it from `/home/research/work` as `/home/research/work/ploinky/bin/ploinky gpu status`, because `ploinky` is not on PATH.
  - It reports `Host GPU: unavailable (NVIDIA driver library libcuda.so.1 is not in the ldconfig cache)`.
  - Cause: `parseLdconfigCache` accepts only entries flagged `x86-64` (`ploinky/ploinky-box/gpuGrant.mjs:239`), and on this host the flag is `AArch64`.
  - With only that filter changed, the rest of discovery succeeds here: 3 device nodes, 5 driver libraries and `nvidia-smi`.
  - The CDI spec, fingerprint and marker carry no architecture data.
- If the agent did run here, admission would pass every model on GPU memory.
  - `readGpu` (`local-llm/src/controller/hardware.mjs`) turns `[N/A]` into `NaN`, so every GPU-memory comparison in `src/controller/admission.mjs` is false.
  - A 500 GiB GGUF (llama.cpp) and a 400 GiB tag (Ollama) are admitted. RAM and disk checks still apply.
  - vLLM gets a `NaN` GPU share and fails at launch (`src/runners/vllm.mjs:115-117`), unless an admin sets the share.

### Multi-arch mechanics

- **`ploinky-node` is an index.** Explorer pins `ploinky-node` by digest `sha256:accd925f…` (`explorer/manifest.json:2`). That digest is an OCI image index with `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` entries, and podman on this Spark resolved it to arm64.
- **`local-llm` is a single manifest.**
  - Its manifest pins a single amd64 image manifest, `b6c79…`, with revision label `95ba10a…`.
  - It was pushed with `provenance: false`, and the OCI referrers API lists no attestations for it.
  - The publish workflow's candidate step already wraps it in an index (`candidate-36131512550-1`), so an `imagetools create` of it plus an arm64 digest is a known operation.
- **Pulls use the host platform.** Ploinky runs `podman pull <image>` with no `--platform` (`ploinky/cli/sandbox/docker/common.js:196`). It adds `--platform` only when `llmRuntime.runtimePolicy.platform` is set (`ploinky/cli/sandbox/docker/containerRuntimePolicy.js:262`).
- **The `ploinky-node` workflow is the model.** `container-image-builds/.github/workflows/publish-ploinky-node-image.yml` builds each platform on its native runner (`ubuntu-24.04`, `ubuntu-24.04-arm`), pushes by digest, proves each platform, and then assembles the index with `docker buildx imagetools create`.
- **Where the amd64 lock-in is.** The runtime base `ploinky-node:24-trixie-tools@sha256:accd925f…` is that same multi-arch index. The amd64 lock-in is the guard `test "${TARGETARCH:-amd64}" = amd64` (`container-image-builds/images/local-llm/Dockerfile:54`) and the x64 downloads that follow it.
- **The dependency cache needs no change.**
  - Ploinky keys it by the image's own `process.arch` (`container-linux-arm64-glibc-node24` vs `container-linux-x64-glibc-node24`).
  - The pin change invalidates each host's cache once, because the stamp records the image reference.

### Box

- **Image.** `ploinky-box:latest` is a multi-arch index; its arm64 variant runs on this Spark (Fedora 44, podman 5.8.2).
- **GPU wiring.**
  - The Box image contains no NVIDIA userland.
  - GPU wiring consists of device nodes, read-only binds of the host's driver libraries under `/usr/local/nvidia`, a hookless CDI spec `ploinky.local/gpu=all`, and a grant marker.
  - The wiring is fixed when the Box is created.
- **Code vs create arguments.**
  - The Box mounts the host's Ploinky checkout read-only at `/opt/ploinky`, so Ploinky code changes reach the Box without an image rebuild.
  - New GPU wiring or Box create arguments take effect only when the Box is replaced, and that restarts the workspace's agents.
- **Constraints for agents:**
  - no `--ipc host`;
  - `/dev/shm` at most `16g`;
  - one 2,048-task pid limit shared by every agent (727 in use with 15 agents);
  - nested cgroups disabled, and the Box itself has no memory limit;
  - no host networking or RDMA (multi-Spark is out of scope by design).
- **Not yet tested.** Nested CDI on arm64 is untested, because the Box has no GPU wiring today (Phase 1).

### Runner availability on arm64

**llama.cpp b11159** (tag commit `6b790a9c291b5d7af3312bbf9f0c558aa023b13e`):

- **Prebuilt assets.** `llama-b11159-bin-ubuntu-cuda-13.4-arm64.tar.gz` (sha256 `258c9dc7c6c02fd2d805ebf9511876ab7b9d7b2d3f0c2166454d682ccae7644b`) and `cudart-llama-b11159-bin-ubuntu-cuda-13.4-arm64.tar.gz` (`34d8602d0084b2498dbf0c436fe2d1d4e54ba577b8d5567eb56990e8fff11bfa`; cudart, cuBLAS and cuBLASLt `.so.13`).
- **How the prebuilt is built.** On `ubuntu-24.04-arm`, in `nvidia/cuda:13.4.1-devel-ubuntu24.04`, with gcc-14 and `GGML_NATIVE=OFF GGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS=ON GGML_BACKEND_DL=ON`. It sets no `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES`, so the default list applies: `75-virtual;80-virtual;86-real;89-real;90-virtual;120a-real;121a-real`, which includes native `sm_121a` code.
- **Driver compatibility.** CUDA 13.x applications run on driver ≥ 580 under minor-version compatibility, provided no PTX JIT is needed. The forward-compatibility package does not apply to GB10.
- **CPU code.** On this CPU (no SME), the `armv8.6_2` variant is selected.
- **CCCL.** A CUDA 13.0 build ships CCCL 3.0.1 and so loses the CUB top-k path, which needs CCCL ≥ 3.2 and which 13.4 has.
- **Still open (Phase 0).** The cubins actually inside the shipped `libggml-cuda.so`, and a run on this driver.

**llama.cpp b11159 options:**

- **Load mode.**
  - `--no-mmap`, `--mmap`, `--mlock` and `--direct-io` were removed in b10875. The option is now `--load-mode {auto,none,mmap,mlock,mmap+mlock,dio}`.
  - `auto` already avoids mmap on an integrated GPU.
  - `dio` reads with O_DIRECT; ggml-org's Spark benchmark uses `mmap 0, dio 1`.
- **Defaults.** `--jinja` is on by default. `-np` defaults to 4 slots with a unified KV cache.
- **MTP exists.** `--spec-type draft-mtp` and `--spec-draft-n-max` (default 3).
- **Mixed KV types are slow.** Flash-attention kernels are compiled only for same-type K/V pairs; a mixed pair converts to f16.
- **Build identity.** Without git metadata a build reports build 0 and commit `unknown`, unless `LLAMA_BUILD_NUMBER` and `LLAMA_BUILD_COMMIT` are set (`cmake/build-info.cmake`).

**NVIDIA's llama.cpp playbook** (`NVIDIA/dgx-spark-playbooks`, `nvidia/llama-cpp`, updated 06/03/2026):

- It clones llama.cpp master without a pin and builds with the host toolkit: `-DGGML_NATIVE=ON -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DGGML_CURL=ON -DGGML_RPC=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=121a-real`. `GGML_CURL` is not an option at b11159.
- It runs with the defaults plus the MTP flags and `--chat-template-kwargs '{"preserve_thinking": true}'`.

**Ollama v0.34.4:**

- **Asset.** `ollama-linux-arm64.tar.zst`: 1,549,684,612 bytes, sha256 `96f50a1192133028cf4e010d8c333f8af14b1505db6be7b2034c11487e7fd7e6`. GB10 is listed as supported.
- **No native sm_121 code.** `cuda_v12` has `sm_120a`, which runs only on 12.0, and `cuda_v13` is PTX-only (`compute_121a`). So the driver JIT-compiles it on first load.
- **Memory.** On integrated GPUs it sizes from MemAvailable and loads with `--load-mode dio`.
- **Install route.** NVIDIA's Ollama playbook installs the unpinned `install.sh`.
- **Still open.** Untested on this host (Phase 0).

**vLLM 0.30.0** (installed on demand):

- **Wheels.**
  - The wheel is `vllm-0.30.0-cp38-abi3-manylinux_2_28_aarch64.whl`.
  - All 196 distributions in the amd64 lock have cp313 aarch64 wheels at the same versions on `files.pythonhosted.org`: none is sdist-only, 3.94 GB in total.
  - torch 2.13 depends on `cuda-toolkit[…]==13.0.3`.
- **Kernels.**
  - vLLM's NVFP4, FP8, Marlin and MoE kernels are built for `12.0f`, which covers 12.1.
  - FlashAttention 2 is PTX only, so the driver JIT-compiles it.
  - torch ships `sm_120` machine code.
  - Triton 3.7.1 maps 12.1 to `sm_121a`, bundles ptxas 13.1.80 and links `-l:libcuda.so.1`.
- **FlashInfer.**
  - FlashInfer 0.6.18 needs a CUDA toolkit (nvcc on PATH) at run time, so offline vLLM turns it off.
  - When the network is reachable, vLLM probes NVIDIA's artifactory to decide FlashInfer paths on SM12x.
- **Known issue.** gpt-oss uses Marlin MXFP4 on SM121, and vLLM #37030 (wrong first Harmony token) is open.
- **Still open.** Untested on this host (Phase 4).

**ik_llama.cpp, TabbyAPI and LM Studio:** x86-only builds today; left out of arm64.

### Model sizes (Hugging Face, for disk planning)

| Model | Size |
| --- | --- |
| gpt-oss-20b MXFP4 GGUF | 12.1 GB |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MTP GGUF, UD-Q4_K_XL / Q8_0 | 22.9 / 37.8 GB |
| Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B Q8_0 | 32.5 GB |
| GLM-4.7-Flash Q8_0 | 31.8 GB |
| gpt-oss-120b MXFP4 GGUF | 63.4 GB, one file |
| Qwen3.5-122B-A10B MXFP4_MOE | 74.7 GB, 3 files |
| `openai/gpt-oss-120b` safetensors (for vLLM) | 65.2 GB |

### Consumer side

- **Discovery.** Soul Gateway discovers the agent through the Router's `/api/router/openai-agent-discovery` and names the model `local-llms/local-llm/default`. It already supports several models per agent through `endpoints.models.command` (later phase).
- **Deadlines.** The chat endpoint's command limit is 600 s (`manifest.json` `timeoutMs: 600000`). Soul Gateway's default request deadline is 120 s.
- **Request fields.** Soul Gateway drops `reasoning_content` and `reasoning_effort` and forwards only some sampling fields. These are later-phase gateway patches, unless decision 9 moves them earlier.

## 4. Work by repository

### A. Ploinky (`github.com/AssistOS-AI/ploinky`) — prerequisite

**1. Required: `parseLdconfigCache` accepts the ldconfig flag of the host architecture.**

- `x64` maps to `x86-64` and `arm64` to `AArch64`; an unknown architecture is refused with a clear reason.
- `discoverNvidiaGpu` takes `arch`, defaulting to `process.arch`.
- Tests pass the architecture explicitly:
  - x64 and arm64 fixtures;
  - an arm64 cache that also lists x86-64 or 32-bit entries;
  - whitespace in the flags;
  - missing libraries, a version mismatch, and an unknown architecture;
  - a round-trip of the arm64 CDI spec, marker and fingerprint that adds no device, mount or privilege.
- Fix the comment at `gpuGrant.mjs:232`; the README has no x86-64 wording.
- **Rollout.** A workspace gets GPU wiring at its next Box replacement (`ploinky start`, `restart` or `update`), which restarts its agents. Do it first in a separate test workspace (Phase 1), then in the live workspace (Phase 3).

**2. Optional, with A1: bind `libnvidia-nvvm70.so.4` when present.** Treat it as a soname-specific exception to the check that driver libraries carry the driver version in their file names: its real file is unversioned, and `libcuda` names it. It exists on every R580 host, x86 included; llama.cpp does not need it.

**3. Only if Phase 4 measures a need: raise the Box's 2,048-task pid limit.** It is a Box create argument, so every workspace's Box is replaced, and Ploinky's Box-identity and E2E rules apply. Keep it a separate change from A1.

**4. Optional: refuse an image before pulling it** when its index has no entry for the host platform, or when it is a single-platform image for another platform, instead of pulling it and failing with `Exec format error`.

- No manifest field; the default stays the host's own platform.
- Consider hosts with binfmt emulation.

**Dropped after review:**

- `/dev/nvidia-uvm-tools`: only profilers need it.
- A `stack` ulimit: local-llm declares no `llmRuntime`, `containerSecurity` has no such key, and no failure needs it.

No Box image change is needed.

### B. `container-image-builds` — the multi-arch image

**1. amd64: reuse `b6c79…` unchanged, through a reuse-and-prove job.**

- The job's input is the pinned digest. It must equal the current pin in `local-llm/manifest.json` and be `linux/amd64`.
- The job re-runs today's proof against that digest with today's expectations: revision label `95ba10a…` instead of `GITHUB_SHA` (`publish-local-llm-image.yml:88`), ik_llama.cpp, CUDA 12 libraries, the LM Studio SDK, and the amd64 runner lock.
- `images/local-llm/Dockerfile`, `sources.lock.json` and `runners.lock.json` stay byte-identical until an amd64 rebuild.
- The shared JavaScript (C) must keep working with this image as published.

**2. arm64: add `images/local-llm/Dockerfile.arm64`.**

- **Same layout as amd64.** Same base (`ploinky-node:24-trixie-tools@sha256:accd925f…`), same `/opt` paths, same `PATH`, and the same `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` (only the granted driver libraries), so the JavaScript does not branch on CPU architecture.
- **llama.cpp: one of two candidates, chosen in Phase 0 (decision 1).** Both carry `121a-real` GPU code and `GGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS` (`armv8.6_2` is selected on this CPU).
  - **L1, prebuilt.** ggml-org's b11159 `ubuntu-cuda-13.4-arm64` pair, pinned by sha256 like the amd64 assets. It runs under CUDA minor-version compatibility.

### C. `local-llms` — agent code with two hardware profiles

**0. First, as a standalone change (Phase 1): treat non-finite GPU memory as unknown.** The GPU is then reported unavailable with a reason, and every Run is refused. Hosts that report numbers see no change.

**1. Hardware snapshot (`src/controller/hardware.mjs`).**

- **Queries.** Keep today's five-field `--query-gpu` call byte-identical. Add a second, optional call for `pci.device_id,compute_cap,addressing_mode,utilization.gpu,power.draw,temperature.gpu`; its failure (an older driver, an unknown field) never disables the GPU.
- **Memory model.**
  - Unified: `memory.total` is `[N/A]` or "Not Supported" and `addressing_mode` is `ATS` or `HMM`; or the PCI device ID is on a known-unified list. That list holds GB10, `0x2E1210DE`, which also covers a future driver that reports numbers.
  - Dedicated: `memory.total` is numeric and the device is not on that list. GH200 is dedicated: it reports ATS with numeric HBM.
  - Anything else is unknown and refused. Do not infer the model from CPU architecture.
- **Unified pool.** Read `/proc/meminfo`: MemTotal and MemAvailable for sizing, MemFree and Cached for display. Never size from `cudaMemGetInfo` or from `nvidia-smi`.
- **Fail closed only on what admission uses.** Utilization, power and temperature are optional telemetry; laptop GPUs report `power.draw` as `[N/A]`.
- **Thread default.** Unchanged, unless sysfs `cpu_capacity` shows cores of different capacity; then it is the number of highest-capacity CPUs (the 10 X925 cores here). A thread count is not affinity: pinning (`--cpu-mask`) is optional and is decided in Phase 0.

**2. Unified admission (`src/controller/admission.mjs`).** llama-server comes first. Ollama is included only if kept, and vLLM stays `incompatible` in the unified profile until Phase 4.

- **What a run needs:** weights + KV cache + compute buffers + MTP allocations when enabled + runner overhead.
- **The KV term follows each runner's contract.** llama-server's `ctxSize` is the whole unified pool (`--kv-unified`), not a per-slot size, so it is not multiplied by the number of slots.
- **Constants and the host reserve come from Phase 0 peak measurements:** download and hash, load, full prefill, parallel slots, and MTP on and off.
- **Verdicts.** `insufficient-now` when the need exceeds MemAvailable minus a floor; `incompatible` when it exceeds MemTotal minus a host reserve.
- **Measured envelope only.** Until the self-calibrating admission of Phase 5, the unified profile admits only configurations inside the envelope Phase 0 measured (weight size, context and slots, MTP). Outside it, Run is refused with that reason.
- **No offload.** No CPU offload and no `nCpuMoe` in this profile.
- **Dedicated unchanged.** The dedicated-memory policy and its constants stay as they are.

**3. Memory containment in the unified profile (`src/controller/deployments.mjs`).** GB10 GPU memory is invisible to RSS, to the OOM score and to memory cgroups, so:

- **OOM priority.** Every runner gets `oom_score_adj=1000` right after spawn and before it loads. This needs no privilege, and children inherit it. A kernel OOM then kills the runner, which frees its GPU memory.
- **An always-on memory guard:**
  - it samples MemAvailable every 250 ms while the model loads and every 2 s once ready, and also watches `/proc/pressure/memory` (`full avg10`);
  - its floor covers the gap between samples: at least max(4 GiB, 5 % of MemTotal), calibrated in Phase 0;
  - if `/proc/meminfo` cannot be read, the runner is stopped.
- **Admission is the primary control,** because one large allocation, such as a KV cache, outruns any sampling. DS003 records this, and records the residual risks:
  - cgroup limits do not bound GPU allocations here;
  - other agents can take memory between admission and load.

**4. Runner and GPU availability (`src/runners/*`, `src/controller/deployments.mjs`), in Phase 2.**

- **`supported` / `unsupportedReason` become run-time properties.** Each adapter computes them at controller start from what the image contains: the executable exists (llama.cpp, ik_llama.cpp, Ollama), or the lock has an entry (vLLM, TabbyAPI, LM Studio). The profile also counts: vLLM is `incompatible` on unified memory until Phase 4.
- **GPU check.** The GPU's compute capability must appear in the image's `gpu_compute_capabilities` (`source.contract`). The amd64 image has no such line, so the check is skipped there, as today.
- **Refuse before downloading.** Run refuses with `runner_unavailable` before any download, and the overview and dashboard say "not available on this platform". Today Run checks only the static `supported` flag and whether the lock can install the runner (`deployments.mjs:796-806`). On an arm64 image that would download a GGUF for ik_llama.cpp and then fail at launch.

**5. llama-server (`src/runners/llamaServer.mjs`, `llamaCpp.mjs`).**

- **Load mode.** Replace `noMmap` / `mlock` with a `loadMode` enum mapped one-to-one to b11159's `--load-mode` (`auto`, `none`, `mmap`, `mlock`, `mmap+mlock`, `dio`).

content.text:
The review session finished revising the plan, and the file matches the hash it reported. The two reviews changed a lot. Here's what matters, then the decisions waiting on you, then two gaps I found.

## Main changes

- **Memory safety got much stricter.** The reviewers measured this on the host: GPU memory on GB10 doesn't show up in process memory figures, the kernel's out-of-memory ranking, or memory limits. So the plan now:
  - marks runners as the first thing the kernel kills when memory runs out;
  - samples free memory every 250 ms while a model loads;
  - only allows setups that Phase 0 actually measured, until self-calibration arrives.
- **My llama.cpp flags were out of date.** `--no-mmap` no longer exists in the pinned build; it's now `--load-mode`, and its `auto` setting already avoids mmap on this GPU. `--jinja` is also on by default now.
- **Unified-memory detection is more robust.** It uses the `[N/A]` memory reading plus GB10's device ID, so it keeps working if a future driver starts reporting numbers. The arm64 image states it's built for GB10, and other arm64 NVIDIA GPUs are refused.
- **x86 users are protected earlier.** The x86 check now happens in Phase 2, before the shared code reaches x86 hosts, not after the image ships.
- **vLLM moved entirely to Phase 4.** The first arm64 image ships without it, because of several open problems (FlashInfer, a network probe, a gpt-oss bug).
- **Ollama became conditional.** It has no native code for this GPU, so its kernels get compiled on first load.
- **Other fixes.**
  - I had undercounted the legacy agents: there are twelve, not eleven.
  - I had planned a `libcuda.so` link for Triton; it turned out unnecessary and was dropped.
  - The first GPU test inside a nested container now happens in a separate test workspace, not the live one.

## Decisions that need you

| # | Question | Needed before |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | First-release models: gpt-oss-20b, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and gpt-oss-120b (about 64 GB of weights at peak), keeping at least 20 GB of disk free | Phase 0 |
| 10 | Retire the legacy translation and reranking services along with the cleanup? | Cleanup |
| 5 | Which x86 GPU machine is the Phase 2 safety check? The RTX 3060 laptop that `local-llm`'s existing measurements came from? | Phase 2 |
| 9 | Do you need 32,000-token answers (what Claude Code asks for) in the first release? If so, the timeout changes to the agent and Soul Gateway move up to Phases 2–3 | Phase 2 |
| 7, 8 | vLLM details: how to handle FlashInfer and its compile caches | Phase 4 only |

Decisions 1 (prebuilt llama.cpp or a source build) and 2 (Ollama) are settled by Phase 0 measurements; the two reviewers disagree on both. You can decide them now if you have a preference, for example if you want Ollama regardless.

## Two gaps in the revision

1. **Removing the dead amd64 image only frees space temporarily.** Phase 0 deletes it (4.9 GB) from the live Box. But the live workspace still enables `local-llm` with that image, and Ploinky pulls any missing image before launching ([common.js:269](ploinky/cli/sandbox/docker/common.js:269)). So the next `ploinky start`, `restart` or `update` re-downloads 4.6 GB (about 10 minutes) and fails again. The space is only really freed until Phase 3 changes the image.
2. **Phase 1's disk use isn't budgeted.** Each workspace's Box keeps its own image store under `<workspace>/.ploinky/box/images`; the live one holds 13 GB. If the test workspace runs Explorer's full set of agents, it downloads all of that again, plus the dead amd64 image. It should enable only `local-llm` with the hand-loaded test image, and Phase 1 needs its own row in the disk table.

The review session says the plan is free to edit again. Should I add these two notes, and record your answers to the decisions above?
